craft_claim: Chinese regulated verse makes tonal pattern and parallelism constitutive of the poem, so euphony is structural rather than optional.

supporting_evidence.location: Wenxin Diaolong, chapters on literary affect and patterning
supporting_evidence.note: Liu Xie frames literature as affection mediated by language and treats pattern and sound as intrinsic to literary form, not applied afterwards.

supporting_evidence.location: analysis of High Tang regulated verse (lushi), tonal and parallel structure
supporting_evidence.note: Owen documents how regulated verse organizes level and oblique tones and parallel couplets into a fixed structure, making sound-pattern a rule of composition.

counterevidence.note: The tonal system has no English equivalent; the sound-structure cannot be reproduced or transferred to stress-timed languages.

scope: Classical Chinese poetry and comparative prosody.
exceptions: Craft claims about tonal parallelism do not transfer into English composition, only the general principle that sound can be structural.
